tested.t1: tested on the U.S. Senate races of 2022 and 2024 in every state but Minnesota; on election night, sized by replays of the 2024 general counted in each state's own order (two also read as totals only)
tested.t2: tested on the governors' races of 2022 and 2024 (MEDSL's copies of the official results, a secondary source); on election night, sized by replays of the 2024 general counted in each state's own order (two also read as totals only)
tested.t3: tested on the other statewide offices of 2022 and 2024 (MEDSL's copies of the official results, a secondary source); on election night, sized by replays of the 2024 general counted in each state's own order (two also read as totals only)

key.r: races by id, the state's prefix ("pre") taken off
key.c: candidates, favourite first: [name as filed, chance, median share, 80% low, 80% high]; a chance is a whole percent from 1 to 99, or ">99" (over 99 percent) or "<1" (under 1 percent); shares in tenths of a percent
key.eq: where nothing on the record separates the candidates: their one shared [chance, median, 80% low, 80% high], and "c" holds the names alone, in alphabetical order (the page says the record gives no reason to favour any of them)
key.s: seats when more than one (the chance is then of finishing among the winners)
key.v: expected voters in the race: [10th, 50th, 90th percentile]
key.x: which past races the method was tested on (a code of "tested")
key.sc: share of the expected vote counted when the model ran (absent before results)
key.t, m, k: the race's own run time, method version and kind where they differ from the file's
key.about: the newest run's inputs and method in plain words ("ran": when the model last ran, though no race may have changed; "t" at the top: when the newest change was made)
key.st: the count's state when the model ran, where it is not "pre": counting (some of the race's precincts in) or done (every precinct in, the counties' last absentee ballots perhaps still to come); absent: none of the race's precincts counted yet
key.k values: pre: the forecast before results; live: the election-night model, from the votes counted so far
key.mg: the likely margin of the top two: the first candidate's share less the second's (the first two of "c"), [median, 80% low, 80% high], in tenths of a percentage point; a range below 0 means the second could finish ahead (absent where several are elected or nothing on the record separates the candidates)
key.ro: where the law asks for more than half the votes: the chance that no candidate passes half (a runoff, or the legislature decides), as a chance cell

about.backtest: Sized by the backtests run on October 10, 2026.
about.count_order: Ohio reports early and absentee ballots received by Election Day first, then Election Day votes; late absentee and provisional ballots come in the canvass. The model never treats the first figures as typical: it compares each county counted with what the forecast expected there, and lets the ballots still to come lean differently from those counted so far.
about.environment: In 10 other states, U.S. Senate polls by members of AAPOR's Transparency Initiative have Democrats running 3.1 points ahead of Kamala Harris's 2024 share of the two-party vote. Applied to Ohio's 2024 presidential result (44.3% Democratic of the two-party vote) and moved a little by Ohio's own member polls, a generic 2026 contest in Ohio stands near 49.6% Democratic, give or take about 1.7 points.
about.gap_start: Where Ohio's figures give county totals only, each county's count is read as two parts, the ballots counted first and those counted last, sized from those shares of each kind of ballot; the model starts from half the gap between the two seen in the past results of the states whose counts split them, and the count itself moves it from there.
about.house: U.S. House: each district's lean is how its precincts voted for President in 2024 against the state (MEDSL's copy of the official returns, a secondary source, placed in districts precinct by precinct), blended with how its 2024 House race went against the top of the ticket; then a sitting member's edge (about 1.0 points) and the district's own error, each sized on the 2024 House races.

about.minor: Candidates outside the two big parties: shares drawn from what such candidates won in 2022 and 2024. Where three or more of them run, their total is likely overstated by a point or two, and the two big parties' shares understated by as much.
about.mix_night: How many of Ohio's ballots were cast early, by mail and on Election Day comes from the Election Assistance Commission's survey of the 2022 election, until Ohio's own count of ballots cast before Election Day is on file here.
about.night: On election night the model compares each county counted so far with what the forecast expected there, learns how the vote has moved (statewide, in each region, with each county's swing between 2022 and 2024 and its Census figures), and estimates the counties and ballots still out. Each race's own results so far set how far it runs ahead of or behind the others.
about.night_now: In the counties counted so far, the Democrats' share of the two-party vote in the statewide races is 0.4 points above what the forecast expected in those same counties.
about.night_tested: Sized by replays of the 2024 general in Florida, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Louisiana and Georgia, counted in each state's own order, North Carolina and Pennsylvania also read as county totals only (80 percent ranges held 95% of the time over 302 race-moments, and at least 86% at every stage of the count; where results give totals only (North Carolina and Pennsylvania replayed that way among them), 87% over 297).
about.not_used: Campaign money, Census figures and ballot position are not used before Election Day: none has been tested on past races here yet.

about.statewide: Statewide races: the state's generic contest plus the office's own pull, sized on the 2022 and 2024 results of every state; a sitting U.S. senator's edge is about 1.4 points. For the other offices the record on file does not say who held the seat in past years, so no holder's edge is added and the spread is wider instead.
about.turnout_night: Expected votes in each county come from 2022's turnout, moved by how complete counties are turning out tonight; the votes still out follow the state's way of counting (precincts still to report, kinds of ballot not yet in, mail still arriving).
